case_prompt:
A 14-year-old girl presented to the pediatric clinic with profound weight loss, fever for one month, and hemoptysis for two days. Family contacts, including both parents, underwent initial screening for chronic respiratory infections and were negative. However, epidemiological inquiry revealed that an immediate neighbor had recently been diagnosed with a severe, drug-resistant chronic pulmonary infection and was receiving treatment at the local referral hospital.

On physical examination, she appeared severely malnourished and chronically ill. Baseline screening for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) was negative. A 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) demonstrated normal sinus rhythm with a normal baseline QT interval. Initial baseline blood counts and routine metabolic panels were within normal limits.

Plain chest radiography demonstrated active pulmonary pathology with marked opacity at the right hilum, a lobulated infiltrate in the left pulmonary apex, nodular opacity at the left hilum, and bilateral perihilar lymphadenopathy.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Infection with Opportunistic Pulmonary Cavitary Disease
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the adolescent presentation with severe wasting/malnutrition, prolonged fever, and apical pulmonary infiltrates with hemoptysis, but excluded by negative HIV screening.
Considered given household risk dynamics, but excluded by comprehensive negative screening of both parents, pinpointing casual/community contact with an infected neighbor.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Her parents showed negative for TB screening. History of tuberculosis contact is her neighbour identified MDR-TB and received treatment in our hospital.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Confirmed by GeneXpert MTB/RIF showing rifampicin-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis, followed by positive mycobacterial culture and line-probe assays demonstrating resistance to isoniazid, rifampicin, and second-line injectables, with preserved susceptibility to fluoroquinolones. Subsequent treatment required substituting bedaquiline with linezolid after marked QTc prolongation developed.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Her X-pert MTB/RIF revealed positive Mycobacterium tuberculosis with Rifampicin resistant. Culture M. tuberculosis was positive, confirming M. tuberculosis resistant to isoniazid and rifampicin on line-probe assay as well as resistant to second-line injectable agents with second-line LPA, but susceptible to the fluoroquinolones. The chest x-ray showed active tuberculosis with opacity at the right hilar, lobulated infiltrate in the left apex, nodular at left hilar, and enlarged bilateral peri-hilar lymph nodes
